findings.claim: The R2 declaration-count guard is a whitespace-exact literal count, so the published bullet "exactly one declaration of each pinned helper" is not what a green run asserts: a second declaration spelled `function docQual () {` (space before the paren) leaves the count at 1 and the run green with two declarations in the file.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1794 `seen = live.count(f"function {fn_name}(")` — a raw substring, while every other comparison in this function goes through `_squash`. Inserting `function docQual () { return ""; }` above `function render(v){` (index.html:883) gives seen==1, body pin byte-equal, passed=True, failures=[]. The same holds for a post-declaration rebind — `docQual = () => "";` or `var docQual = function(){ return ""; };` above render(), and `coverageStrip = () => "";` — all green, all neuter the qualifier at runtime. Falsifies bullet 2 of eval_adapter.py:1662 and of the case `ceiling`.
findings.repro: Copy index.html, insert `function docQual () { return ""; }` immediately above `function render(v){`, run ui-confidence-honesty with input.file pointed at the copy -> passed=True. Orchestrator-confirmed, as was the `docQual = () => "";` rebind.
findings.acceptance: Either the count is whitespace-tolerant (`len(re.findall(rf"function\s+{fn_name}\s*\(", live))`) with a spaced-duplicate mutation added to pr53_mutation_probe.py and watched green-then-red, or the bullet reads "exactly one declaration spelled `function <name>(`" rather than "exactly one declaration".

findings.claim: The widened scan considers only the NEAREST preceding `${`, so a mention inside an enclosing interpolation that contains an earlier nested `${...}` is skipped entirely — a rendering spelling that prints a bare number and stays green, falsifying the rewritten first bullet.
findings.evidence: src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py:1742 `opened = live.rfind("${", 0, m.start())` followed by `if i <= m.start(): continue` at :1751 — when the nearest `${` closed early the mention is dropped rather than searched further back. A sidebar badge spelled ``conf ${(it.evidence?.warnings||[]).length ? `⚠ ${esc(it.evidence.warnings[0])}` : it.confidence}`` renders a bare confidence on the else branch and gives passed=True. The mention IS inside an interpolation whose whole `${...}` is not the pinned marker, so eval_adapter.py:1660-1662 and the identical sentence in the case `ceiling` are literally false. The brace walk is also not string/regex aware and that ceiling is unstated (`_js_block`'s docstring states its equivalent).
findings.repro: Copy index.html, insert the nested-template span above; run_case on ui-confidence-honesty with input.file set to the copy -> passed True. Variants ``conf ${`${""}` + it.confidence}`` and ``conf ${[`${""}`, it.confidence].join("")}`` are also green.
findings.acceptance: Either the walk retries successively earlier `${` until one encloses the mention (with a nested-template mutation added to the probe, watched green-then-red), or the code comment and the bullet name the ceiling out loud: only the nearest preceding `${` is considered.
